Identity, roles, staffing and authority

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Separate identity from business authority
  • Explain staffing gates
  • Trace revocation

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01IdP / login
  2. 02Tenant actor
  3. 03Role + staffing
  4. 04ctrl-* decision
  5. 05Domain maker-checker
  6. 06Attributed mutation

1. Authentication is not authorization

Sessions, API keys and federation establish an actor.

Tenant roles and feature staffing determine what that actor may do.

Domain maker-checker rules remain authoritative even when IAM says a user can reach a route.

2. Control-engine authority

Protected staff mutations are classified and evaluated through the isolated control rules engine. Unknown or unavailable control decisions deny in active mode.

3. Revocation

SCIM/federation lifecycle, staff status, delegation expiry, queue assignment and digital-worker installation state all affect authority. Revocation must stop future work while retaining historical attribution.
